## bioRxiv
An MCP server for accessing bioRxiv and medRxiv preprint servers.

This server provides:
- Tools: Search preprints, get preprint details, list subject categories
- Prompts: Analyze preprint methodology and findings

bioRxiv is a preprint server for biological sciences operated by Cold Spring
Harbor Laboratory. It hosts research manuscripts that have NOT undergone peer
review. This server wraps the official bioRxiv API to provide structured access
to preprint metadata, abstracts, and full-text PDFs.

TOOL SELECTION GUIDE:
• search_preprints: Find preprints by date range and/or subject category (no keyword, author, or full-text search) - primary discovery tool
• get_preprint: Get full details for a specific preprint by DOI
• get_categories: List available subject categories for filtering
• search_published_preprints: Find preprints that have been formally published in journals
• funder_search: Find preprints by funding source (NIH, etc.)
• get_statistics: Usage and submission statistics

MULTI-TOOL WORKFLOWS:
For comprehensive literature analysis:
1. Use search_preprints to find relevant preprints by date range and category
2. Use get_preprint for detailed information on promising results
3. Use search_published_preprints to check if preprints have been peer-reviewed and published
4. Use funder_search to identify research funding patterns in a field

For tracking research trends:
1. Use get_categories to identify relevant subject areas
2. Use search_preprints with date filters for recent activity
3. Use get_statistics to understand submission volumes

## Claude_Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## Consensus
Consensus is a research paper search engine: relevance-ranked semantic search over 400M+ peer-reviewed papers (Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, PubMed). Use the `search` tool to look up papers for a scientific query; it takes plain-language queries and returns ranked paper records. When presenting search results, you MUST cite papers inline using their numbered references from the tool result (e.g. [1], [2], [3]). When discussing findings, always attribute them to specific papers: 'Caffeine improves endurance performance [1] and reduces perceived exertion [3].' At the end of your response, list all cited papers as numbered references with their titles hyperlinked to the URLs from the tool result: [1] [Paper Title](url) (Authors, Year, Journal, Citations). Use the exact paper URLs from the tool result — do not modify, shorten, or regenerate them. Do not omit paper links or summarize results without citing specific papers. IMPORTANT: Some search results end with a sign-up, upgrade, or usage message. When a result has one, you MUST include it at the END of your response word-for-word: do not omit, shorten, or rephrase it. When a result has none, do not add one: never write your own upgrade prompt, search count, or Consensus link. Batch at most 3 search calls at a time to avoid rate limits. For a broad request (a review, screening, finding everything on a topic), make one search with a large page_size rather than many narrower searches. If you receive a rate limit error, wait 30 seconds before retrying. Do NOT apply search filters (year_min, year_max, study_types, domain, human, sample_size_min, sjr_max, controlled, sjr_min, citation_min, open_access, country) unless the user explicitly requests them or clearly expresses intent to narrow results. If the user asks a research question without mentioning filtering criteria, call search with only the query parameter.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

## Google_Drive
This is an MCP server provided by Drive API. The server provides tools for developers to build LLM applications on top of Drive.

1. Use search_preprints to find relevant preprints by date range and category
2. Use get_preprint for detailed information on promising results
3. Use search_published_preprints to check if preprints have been peer-reviewed and published
4. Use funder_search to identify research funding patterns in a field

For tracking research trends:
1. Use get_categories to identify relevant subject areas
2. Use search_preprints with date filters for recent activity
3. Use get_statistics to understand submission volumes


## Claude_Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## Consensus
Consensus is a research paper search engine: relevance-ranked semantic search over 400M+ peer-reviewed papers (Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, PubMed). Use the `search` tool to look up papers for a scientific query; it takes plain-language queries and returns ranked paper records. When presenting search results, you MUST cite papers inline using their numbered references from the tool result (e.g. [1], [2], [3]). When discussing findings, always attribute them to specific papers: 'Caffeine improves endurance performance [1] and reduces perceived exertion [3].' At the end of your response, list all cited papers as numbered references with their titles hyperlinked to the URLs from the tool result: [1] [Paper Title](url) (Authors, Year, Journal, Citations). Use the exact paper URLs from the tool result — do not modify, shorten, or regenerate them. Do not omit paper links or summarize results without citing specific papers. IMPORTANT: Some search results end with a sign-up, upgrade, or usage message. When a result has one, you MUST include it at the END of your response word-for-word: do not omit, shorten, or rephrase it. When a result has none, do not add one: never write your own upgrade prompt, search count, or Consensus link. Batch at most 3 search calls at a time to avoid rate limits. For a broad request (a review, screening, finding everything on a topic), make one search with a large page_size rather than many narrower searches. If you receive a rate limit error, wait 30 seconds before retrying. Do NOT apply search filters (year_min, year_max, study_types, domain, human, sample_size_min, sjr_max, controlled, sjr_min, citation_min, open_access, country) unless the user explicitly requests them or clearly expresses intent to narrow results. If the user asks a research question without mentioning filtering criteria, call search with only the query parameter.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

## Google_Drive
This is an MCP server provided by Drive API. The server provides tools for developers to build LLM applications on top of Drive.

Derive the times from the preserved transcript (`git grep -n -F "yes, translation runs before judgment" -- transcripts`).

**Owner's words, quoted (typed):**

> "we research, we record, we verify we recorded things accurately, we evaluate things in context with other related things, we synthesize then show"
>
> "base is the substitute for me asking for a research topic directly"
>
> "i only know english, so the base has to record all the translation work for me"
>
> "i don't want to have to constantly map and cross-reference disability identities vs access needs vs ICF codes, so the base needs to get that ready for me too"
>

>
> "this is also why we need to be able to convert units etc"
>
> "this project will die upon itself if it doesn't treat disability identities properly. they are going to be by far the most common lens upon which people will navigate the repository"
>
> "yes, translation runs before judgment"

**Readings.**

- [ASSUMPTION: "yes, translation runs before judgment" answers the coordinator's question whether translation of every non-English source and figure is to be recorded before the judgment stage evaluates it, replacing the default of `translation: default_stage: synthesis` in `governance/pipeline-contract.yaml` (set on the owner's words of 2026-11-12, "we can set a rule for synthesis to translate") — basis: the question put to the owner, and rule 0].

(2) An English rendering is not written into `claimed_value` or `claimed_unit`. (3) Treat a disability identity as the first lens of the repository: an identity with no ICF code, and an identity with no recorded need, is a gap to close and not a state to leave. ## Owner statements 2026-11-20 (third) — the project is a database and a pipeline, kept as simple as possible; the content of the CLAUDE.md rewrite

Given in the session `session_2026-11-20-unregistered-map-codes` (https://claude.ai/code/session_01Ub36iQWmsqeLLsdnXfD7Pu), in typed messages while the coordinator reported an Opus adjudication of the core against the machinery and an antagonist audit of it. > "this entire infrastructure is just trying to formalize asking a Claude session to do research on a topic"
>
> "i have just spent a huge amount of time trying to harness an LLM through gates/scripts/github/etc instead of just using it to translate things i can't read"

>

**The content of the CLAUDE.md rewrite, recorded so a later session can write it.** Source: the Opus adjudication of 2026-11-20 and the antagonist's audit of it, read by the coordinator. **This is a proposal. The owner has not approved it, and `CLAUDE.md` is unchanged by this entry.** Its sections, in order:

1. **Goal.** The owner's goal sentence verbatim, then one line: a thinking tool, not an authority; the database records research properly and a pipeline processes it; `base` is the owner's request layer, standing where the owner would otherwise ask for a topic directly.
2. **The things never to get wrong.** (a) Fetch before you write any author, title or figure; a bibliographic field is never written from memory when a payload is in hand. 5. **Derive, do not type, a number** (rules 7a and 8, condensed).
6. **Pointers** to doctrine, the tier system, the rulings ledger and the working-rules file.

**Moved to a referenced working-rules file:** rules 0, 1, 4, 5, 6, 9 and 10; section 3 (the layers and the spine); section 7 (traps); section 8. **Deleted:** the Layer-0 preamble, rule 7 (merged into 7a), the sentence that the stage display form is derived by `stage_label()` (no such function exists: `git grep -n stage_label -- scripts governance .claude skills` finds none), and the embedded "Proof" narratives (`git log -p CLAUDE.md` holds them).

**Two constraints the audit found.** `scripts/audit/claude_md_spine.py` pins the SPINE line, so that line stays in `CLAUDE.md` or the blocking check moves with it. Comments in scripts cite `CLAUDE.md` rules by number (for example "rule 4", "section 5(c)"), so renumbering breaks them silently; sweep them first (rule 4 names prose callers as unswept). **Size,** measured and never typed: `[ $(wc -w < CLAUDE.md) -le $(( $(git show origin/main:CLAUDE.md | wc -w) / 4 )) ]`.

**What the owner approves, and what a session may do.** The owner approves the goal sentence, rule 0, rule 9, the tier and Co-1 definitions, and the fate of the layer model. A session may reorder and reword process rules, traps and command lists.

**The simplicity rule these words state, for any session that adds anything:** each addition names the existing thing it replaces or deletes and what reads it; a new exception is a reason to change the rule, not to add a guard (CLAUDE.md section 8 already says the first half).

CONDITION: any session editing `CLAUDE.md`, adding a table, verb, check, script or exception, or planning the remediation work.
ACTION: (1) Do not rewrite `CLAUDE.md` until the owner approves the content above; then write it from this entry and the audit, with the size command. (2) Before adding apparatus, state what it replaces and what reads it. (3) Treat the proposal's sections and moves as unratified until the owner's words approve them.

# T-112  Translate the held non-English text that synthesis needs

_One task, one pull request. Read `CLAUDE.md` first; beyond it this file is self-contained. Index, order and the owner decision register: `workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/REMEDIATION-WORKPLAN.md`. Evidence base: `workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/01-handshake-ledger.md`, as corrected by `scratchpad/session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit/audit/fa-corrections-for-suite.md` (where they differ, the corrections govern). Every number in this file was read on 2026-11-12 and is given with the command that produces it: re-run the command; do not trust the number._

**Pilot status.** Not piloted. Three tasks of this plan were executed in scratch clones (T-006, T-008, T-010) and the defects they showed in the task files were corrected in every file by one generator; this file's own steps have not been executed by anyone. Its evidence command was run on 2026-11-12 and printed what section 3 states. Expect to find a defect in this file, and report it rather than work around it.

## 1. Identity

| | |
|---|---|
| Task | T-112 |
| Title | Translate the held non-English text that synthesis needs |
| Wave | research |
| Layer (CLAUDE.md §3) | 3 |
| Kind | **RESEARCH** (CLAUDE.md rule 10: tooling and research never share a pull request) |
| Executor | Sonnet-class (drafting and recording; a review verdict is an Opus-class act in a later session) |
| Traces to | REQ-104 (owner statement 2026-11-12, ninth) in `scratchpad/session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit/audit/hs-improvement-programme.md` |

## 2. Preconditions

- **The integration base.** This workplan must be on the branch you start from. If the workplan's pull request is merged, that is `origin/main`. Until then it is the workplan branch, `origin/ccr-408aaa9b-z3e4s0` (if that name is gone: `git branch -r --contains "$(git log --all --format=%H -1 -- workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/REMEDIATION-WORKPLAN.md)"`). Every command in this file uses `$BASE`, set by the first line of the set-up block, and never a literal `origin/main`: on a base that lacks the workplan, a diff against `origin/main` contains the whole workplan and every gate and count is about the wrong change.
- **Tasks that must be merged to the integration base first:** T-049 merged. Check by running that task's own after-test (its section 6), or `git log "$BASE" --oneline | grep -F "<that task's commit subject>"`.
- **Owner decisions:** none outstanding. The decisions this task needed are resolved under delegation (next bullet); none is still the owner's.
- **Delegated resolutions this task rests on.** OD-02: the target language is English, for display only; it does not fix the language synthesis compares in. OD-30: any model may draft and record a translation, recording itself as translator; a reader sees one only after an Opus-class instance other than the translator reviews it. Each is a resolution by an Opus-class model under the owner's delegation of 2026-11-12: not the owner's words, reversible by the owner, and read only through the ledger's gate (`grep -n -F "Convention 2026-11-12 — how a delegated resolution" references/project-standards.md`). Run it before you start and again before you open the pull request; if any line prints CLOSED, stop (section 9):
```
gate(){ s=$(grep -F "$1 STATUS:" references/project-standards.md | tail -1); c=$(grep -F "$1 CHECK:" references/project-standards.md | tail -1); case "$s" in *"ANSWERED BY THE OWNER"*) echo "$1 OPEN (owner)";; *"RESOLVED UNDER DELEGATION"*) case "$c" in *"not required"*|*confirmed*) echo "$1 OPEN (delegated; ${c#*CHECK: })";; *) echo "$1 CLOSED (check: ${c:-none})";; esac;; *) echo "$1 CLOSED (${s:-no status line})";; esac; }
for n in OD-02 OD-30; do gate $n; done
```
- **Tests that must be red (or green) before you start:** AT-107 green (the verbs exist); `select count(*) from translations` is 0. (`AT-` numbers are the acceptance tests of `scratchpad/session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit/audit/hs-improvement-programme.md` §4, §7 and §9 and of `scratchpad/session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit/audit/td-requirements-and-interface-spec.md`; the test this task must turn is restated in full in section 6, so you do not need to open either.)
- **Set-up.**

```
cd /home/user/guidebook
bash .claude/hooks/ensure-deps.sh && python3 -c "import pydantic, jsonschema, yaml"
git fetch origin
W=$(git log --remotes --format=%H -1 -- workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline); BASE=$(git branch -r --contains "$W" --format='%(refname:short)' | grep -x origin/main || git branch -r --contains "$W" --format='%(refname:short)' | head -1); echo "BASE=$BASE"
git switch -c task/t-112-translate-held-text "$BASE"
STEM=session_$(date -u +%Y-%m-%d)-<slug>            # the session stem: bare in the database, with .md for emit_data_migration --session
export SCRATCH="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/guidebook-t-112" && mkdir -p "$SCRATCH" && cp data/guidebook.db "$SCRATCH/s.db" && cp data/guidebook.db "$SCRATCH/t.db"   # s.db is the batch's working copy; t.db is for probes
```
- **Shell variables do not survive from one tool call to the next in this harness.** Write the stem down once and begin every later command block by setting `BASE`, `STEM` and `SCRATCH` again to the same values.
- **Real execution:** open with `/session-open` (it sets `scratchpad/CURRENT` to the stem and creates the folder of the same name), then `/orient`. Follow `skills/run-pipeline_SKILL.md`. **Pilot or dry run** (a scratch clone): skip `/session-open`, stay on the branch you were given, do the work on the scratch copy only, and stop before the write path below.
- Work only on the scratch copy and point every call at it inline:
```
GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH="$SCRATCH/s.db" python3 scripts/db.py <verb> ... --session "$STEM"
```
- Land the rows only by the write path, after the work is finished:
```
python3 scripts/research/emit_batch_sql.py --scratch "$SCRATCH/s.db" --out "$SCRATCH/batch.sql"
python3 scripts/emit_data_migration.py --session "$STEM.md" --summary "<what the batch is>" --input "$SCRATCH/batch.sql"
python3 scripts/migrate_db.py
python3 scripts/migrate_db.py --rebuild "$SCRATCH/rebuilt.db"      # must exit 0
```
Research batches are serial: if another research batch merged after you copied the database, `emit_batch_sql.py` refuses ("copied from a different base"). Do not force it; start again from the new base.

## 3. The problem, in the guidebook's terms

Figures quoted in Dutch, Finnish, Japanese, Korean, Swedish and other languages sit beside English ones under the same parameter and cannot be discussed together by a reader, or checked by the owner, who does not read all of them.

**Evidence command** (run from the repository root, after the set-up block so that `$SCRATCH` exists; it reads the canonical database read-only or works on a copy):

```
python3 -I -c "import sqlite3;c=sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro',uri=True);print(c.execute(\"select upper(coalesce(e.lang_detected,'?')), count(*) from source_value_extractions x join evidence_sources e using(ref_id) group by 1 order by 2 desc\").fetchall())"
```

**Expected output today:** Figures by the recorded language of their source; several languages other than English, and many sources with no language recorded.

If the output differs, the ground has moved: stop (section 9). Ids that appear in this command are probes read on 2026-11-12; where the command derives an id by query, that is deliberate, and a test you write must do the same (section 6).

## 4. The change

Order of preference, from CLAUDE.md §8: do nothing and say why; change a rule or convention; reuse what exists; delete the cause; only then add the smallest code that closes the defect.

1. For the parameters about to be synthesised first (ramp gradient, then ramp run length), request and record a translation of each non-English `claim_text` with the verbs of T-049, from the stage the session is working in. The original is never edited. Each row records its translator. A figure in the translation must be the row's verified figure: the verb refuses otherwise.
2. Do not translate a term into a new term, and do not write a translation into any column that holds a source's wording. Titles, observed phrases and clauses follow when a stage needs them; this batch does quotations. A form (a `term_aliases` row) cannot be translated until T-028 has merged: T-049's `request-translation` refuses a pointer into a table whose key is composite, and `term_aliases` is keyed `(term_id, alias, language)` until T-028 gives it `form_id` (T-049 section 4 item 6).
3. **Who translates and who reviews (OD-30, resolved under delegation).** Record yourself as translator (`--translator-kind model --translator-name <your model id>`). Do not record a review verdict on your own translation: `review-translation --verdict reviewed` is a later Opus-class session's act, by an instance other than the translator. Target language English (OD-02), for display; synthesis may read these as aids.

**What reads what this task adds or changes:** the synthesis discussion; render (reviewed translations only)

**Data migration.** This task lands rows through `scripts/emit_data_migration.py`, which names the file itself; never type a migration name or number, and never edit the file it writes. The pull request contains no schema migration and no file under `scripts/` other than that one `scripts/migrations/data_*` file.

## 5. Caller sweep

A research task renames nothing and changes no code, so the sweep that applies is the one for prose that restates a fact your rows change (CLAUDE.md rule 7a). For each row id, code or value you change, search the reading surface and the governance prose, and correct a sentence your rows make false (or stop, if correcting it is not research):

```
V='<the id, code or value you changed>'
git grep -n -F -e "$V" -- governance architecture CLAUDE.md references skills ':(exclude)references/project-standards.md' ':(exclude)references/search-log'
```

Structures this task touches, for orientation: `translations`. The ledger (`references/project-standards.md`), `sessions/` and committed migrations are records and are never edited.

## 6. Verification

**Red before, green after.** `translation_pointer_audit` passes with `EXAMINED:` above 0; every non-English `claim_text` of the chosen parameters has a current translation (`v_translations_current`); every original cell's hash is unchanged.

**Fixtures.** Probes run on `$SCRATCH/t.db`; the batch's own rows are written on `$SCRATCH/s.db` and reach `data/guidebook.db` only through the write path of section 2.

**The gates, once each:**

```
W=$(git log --remotes --format=%H -1 -- workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline); BASE=$(git branch -r --contains "$W" --format='%(refname:short)' | grep -x origin/main || git branch -r --contains "$W" --format='%(refname:short)' | head -1)
python3 scripts/audit/research_batch_dod.py --session "$STEM" > "$SCRATCH/dod.txt" 2>&1; echo "rc=$?"; grep -E 'EXAMINED|BLOCKED|PASS|FAIL' "$SCRATCH/dod.txt" | tail -8   # the research gate
scripts/preflight.sh --base "$BASE" --explain > "$SCRATCH/gate.txt" 2>&1; echo "rc=$?"; grep -E '^(RESULT|PREFLIGHT|SELFTEST)|FAIL|NOTHING-IN-SCOPE' "$SCRATCH/gate.txt"
```
- **Run each once, after the migration is applied and before the commit.** `preflight.sh` runs the selftest and `run_checks.py --changed-from`; do not run `run_checks.py` separately, and never `--all`.
- **Proof that each gate examined something.** A check scoped to a session id that matches no row passes having read nothing. Confirm the stem is the one stored on your rows. The tables a batch writes carry `created_by_session` and `updated_by_session`; for each table this task writes, `python3 -I -c "import sqlite3,sys;c=sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro',uri=True);print(c.execute('select count(*) from '+sys.argv[2]+' where created_by_session=? or updated_by_session=?',(sys.argv[1],sys.argv[1])).fetchone())" "$STEM" <table>` must be above 0 after the migration is applied. `research_batch_dod` prints its own `EXAMINED:` lines: read them in `dod.txt`. A passing check prints no `EXAMINED:` line in `gate.txt`; any check under `NOTHING-IN-SCOPE` there has not passed. `migration_reproducibility` compares row counts only, so an UPDATE is invisible to it: also run `python3 scripts/audit/migration_reproducibility.py --deep`, which compares every row.

## 7. Commit

Commit **after** the gate of section 6 is clean.
```
git add -A . ':!transcripts' ':!*commands.jsonl'      # add the two append-only logs only at a natural break (CLAUDE.md rule 6)
git commit -m "run-pipeline: translate held non-English quotations for the first parameters [$(date -u '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M')]" -m "<body: what changed, the evidence commands and their output, the callers the sweep found and what was done to each>" -m "<the attribution trailers your own session instructions give: a Co-Authored-By line and a Claude-Session line>"
```
The format is `{skill-name}: {action} [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM]`, timestamp last, taken from `date -u`. Do not copy trailers from this file; use the ones your session was given.

## 8. What you must NOT do

- Do not write `data/guidebook.db` directly. Rows land only by the write path of section 2.
- Do not hand-write SQL against a table a `db.py` verb can reach. A table no verb reaches is a gap to file (`db.py add-gap`), not a licence.
- Do not put tooling in this pull request: no schema migration, no new verb, no new check, no edit under `scripts/`, `schemas/`, `.github/` or `skills/` (CLAUDE.md rule 10). A writer gap found on the way is filed and left.
- Do not write a bibliographic field from memory when a payload is in hand; do not mark a source verified that was not re-retrieved; never leave `verification_status` NULL.
- Do not move, round or re-key an adjudicated figure. Do not back-translate a term. Do not delete an empty search.
- Do not author a specification row (`specifications`, read through `v_best_practice`; CLAUDE.md §6's `best_practice_synthesis` names a table not in the schema: superseded in part by TERM-RESOLUTION-PLAN §2, 2026-11-14) or synthesis prose below the Opus floor.
- Do not decide doctrine (mission, audience, CRPD posture, population taxonomy, evidence-tier definitions, jurisdiction scope, licensing, trajectory). Stop instead.
- Do not treat any `[A-Z]-NN` code as a container, an example or a name.
- Do not run `scripts/run_checks.py --all`, `scripts/bootstrap.sh`, or `pip install -r requirements.txt`. Do not push to `main`, rebase or force-push. Do not subscribe to pull-request activity or schedule check-ins.
- Do not hand-type a count into any file or message; write the command that computes it.

## 9. Stop conditions

Stop, change nothing further, and report (what you ran, what you saw, what you expected) when any of these happens:
- a precondition in section 2 is not met, or an owner decision named there is unanswered or answered in another form;
- the evidence command in section 3 does not give today's expected output (the defect may already be fixed, or the ground has moved);
- the red test is not red before the change, or is not green after it, after one honest attempt;
- the sweep of section 5 finds a caller (as defined there) that you cannot repair without adding something section 4 does not name. A caller you can repair is repaired and listed; a mention is left;
- a check or test that was green in the before-run is red in the after-run, at any level (the test files are registered as advisory, so the gate will not stop you: the before-and-after comparison is what does);
- `sha256sum data/guidebook.db` changes when this task has no migration, or the rebuild does not reproduce the database when it has one;
- you would have to guess a value, a vocabulary term, a name or an owner's intent.
- the delegation gate of section 2 prints CLOSED for a decision this task rests on (the owner has reversed it, a correction has withdrawn it, or its independent check is not recorded); a delegated resolution is never the owner's words;

## 10. Rollback

Before the migration is applied: delete the scratch copy; nothing has changed. After it is committed: a data migration is append-only and immutable; correct a wrong row with a compensating migration written through the same verbs (retire, supersede, amend), never by editing or deleting the file.

## 11. Adversarial pass and pull request

Real execution only; a pilot stops after section 7.
1. Run `/adversarial` once on the finished diff (a read-only critic attacks the claim, then you repair). One pass; no pass on the pass. For a research task the pass is recorded in the database with `db.py record-adversarial-pass` and closed with `close-adversarial-pass`.
2. Run `/batch-done`; it is the only definition of finished.
3. Push the branch. Open the pull request **last**, once, against the integration base (section 2). Title = the commit subject. Body: the problem; the evidence before and after; each caller the sweep found and what was done to it; each check you ran with its `EXAMINED:` line, before and after; the code-size line; what was not verified. End the body with the pull-request attribution line your session instructions give.
4. Immediately after creating the pull request call `unsubscribe_pr_activity` for it (creating a pull request subscribes the session by itself). Do not watch it, do not poll, do not schedule a reminder. Push nothing afterwards except a deliberate change; the final push is never `[skip ci]`.
5. One pull request merges at a time. If another task's pull request merged while you worked, take it with `git merge "$BASE"` after `git fetch origin` (never rebase) and, if you carry a schema migration, derive its number again by the rule in section 4.

# --- translations (T-049) ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# A translation POINTS at the cell it translates (translations.source_*) and never replaces or copies it; the
# original is untouched by construction. The default stage a request falls due at is a RULE held once in
# governance/pipeline-contract.yaml, read through `_translation_contract` and computed when listed, never stored
# and never written in this block. The pointer is resolved by `dbcore.read_cell` and nothing else.


def _translation_contract(contract_path=None):
    """The pipeline contract through its schema model: the one reader of the translation rule and of the stage ids.
    `contract_path` exists so a test can load a changed copy; the CLI does not expose it."""
    from schemas.pipeline_contract import PipelineContract
    return PipelineContract.load(contract_path or dbcore.REPO_ROOT / "governance" / "pipeline-contract.yaml")


def _translation_stage(contract, stage, flag):
    ids = [st.id for st in contract.stages]
    if stage not in ids:
        raise Refusal(f"{flag} {stage!r} is not a stage id of governance/pipeline-contract.yaml "
                      f"({', '.join(ids)}). Nothing was written.")
    return stage


def _cell_language(conn, table, key):
    """The language the pointed row records: its own `lang_detected`, else its own `language` (whichever the table
    has and is not NULL), else, when it has a `ref_id`, that source's `evidence_sources.lang_detected`. None when the
    row leads to none. Compared upper-cased by the caller: stored values are mixed-case."""
    cols = {c[1] for c in conn.execute('PRAGMA table_info("%s")' % table)}
    pk = dbcore.single_key(conn, table)
    for col in ("lang_detected", "language"):
        if col in cols:
            r = conn.execute('SELECT "%s" FROM "%s" WHERE "%s" = ?' % (col, table, pk), (key,)).fetchone()
            if r and r[0]:
                return r[0]
    if "ref_id" in cols:
        r = conn.execute('SELECT e.lang_detected FROM evidence_sources e JOIN "%s" t ON t.ref_id = e.ref_id '
                         'WHERE t."%s" = ?' % (table, pk), (key,)).fetchone()
        if r and r[0]:
            return r[0]
    return None


def translation_sha256(text):
    """The hash of a cell's text, as `translations.source_sha256` holds it. One home: the verbs and the audit."""
    return hashlib.sha256(text.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


def translation_claimed_value(conn, source_table, source_column, source_row_key):
    """The verified `claimed_value` of the figure whose `claim_text` a translation translates, else None. It is the
    numeral of a number the source may write in words, so the translation may state it."""
    if (source_table, source_column) != ("source_value_extractions", "claim_text"):
        return None
    r = conn.execute("SELECT claimed_value FROM source_value_extractions WHERE extraction_id = ?",
                     (source_row_key,)).fetchone()
    return r[0] if r else None


def translation_number_gaps(original, translation, claimed_value=None):
    """(dropped, added): the numbers `original` states that `translation` does not, and the numbers `translation`
    states that neither `original` nor `claimed_value` does. The fidelity rule of `record-translation`.

    The reader is `retrieval_log.number_tokens` (T-008). Both texts first pass through `_cjk_to_arabic` (so 十二分の一
    states 12 and 1 and a correct `1:12` is not an added figure) and are read on the quote side, where the operands of
    a symbol ratio and the pieces of a space-grouped number count as stated. The sets of readings are compared, not
    ratio tokens and not counts: a number is matched when one of its readings is a reading of some number of the other
    (an ambiguous `1.200` matches 1.2 or 1200), and a number stated twice need not be stated twice. `claimed_value`
    is read on the claim side (no CJK step, no operands).
    """
    rl = _retrieval_log()

    def stated(text, **kw):
        return [set(readings) for kind, readings, _ in rl.number_tokens(text, **kw) if kind == "num"]

    def shown(sets):
        return sorted({"/".join(sorted(str(x) for x in s)) for s in sets})

    orig = stated(_cjk_to_arabic(original or ""), quote_side=True)
    trans = stated(_cjk_to_arabic(translation or ""), quote_side=True)
    extra = stated(str(claimed_value)) if claimed_value is not None else []
    return (shown(o for o in orig if not any(o & t for t in trans)),
            shown(t for t in trans if not any(t & o for o in orig + extra)))


def _current_translation(conn, table, column, key, language, excluding=None):
    """The id and status of the current (translated or reviewed, not retired) translation of this cell into this
    language other than `excluding`, else None."""
    return conn.execute(
        "SELECT translation_id, status FROM v_translations_current WHERE source_table=? AND source_column=? "
        "AND source_row_key=? AND target_language=? AND translation_id IS NOT ?",
        (table, column, key, language, excluding)).fetchone()


def _refuse_second_translation(conn, table, column, key, language, excluding, context):
    held = _current_translation(conn, table, column, key, language, excluding)
    if held:
        raise Refusal(f"{context}: this cell is already translated into {language} as translation "
                      f"{held['translation_id']} ({held['status']}). A corrected translation is a new row that "
                      f"retires the old one: record-translation --supersedes {held['translation_id']}. "
                      f"Nothing was written.")


def _require_translation_session(session, context):
    if not (session or "").strip():
        raise Refusal(f"{context}: --session is required and may not be blank. Nothing was written.")


def _open_translation_request(conn, table, column, row_key, language, stage, due_stage, contract, session, context,
                              replacing=None):
    """Validate a pointer against the live schema and open the request, or find the one already open for the same
    pointer, hash and language. Returns (translation_id, created)."""
    text, key, why = dbcore.read_cell(conn, table, column, row_key)
    if why:
        raise Refusal(f"{context}: the pointer does not resolve: {why}. Nothing was written.")
    _refuse_retired_cell(conn, table, key, context)
    lang = _check_language(conn, language, "translation", "--target-language")
    src = _cell_language(conn, table, key)
    if src and src.strip().upper() == lang.upper():
        raise Refusal(f"{context}: the pointed row is recorded in {src.strip().upper()}, the target language. "
                      f"There is nothing to translate. Nothing was written.")
    _translation_stage(contract, stage, "--stage")
    if due_stage is not None:
        _translation_stage(contract, due_stage, "--due-stage")
    _refuse_second_translation(conn, table, column, key, lang, replacing, context)
    sha = translation_sha256(text)
    open_one = conn.execute(
        "SELECT translation_id FROM translations WHERE source_table=? AND source_column=? AND source_row_key=? "
        "AND source_sha256=? AND target_language=? AND status='requested' AND superseded_by_translation_id IS NULL",
        (table, column, key, sha, lang)).fetchone()
    if open_one:
        return open_one[0], False
    row = {"source_table": table, "source_column": column, "source_row_key": key, "source_sha256": sha,
           "target_language": lang, "status": "requested", "requested_at_stage": stage, "due_stage": due_stage}
    row.update(dbcore.stamp_for(conn, "translations", session))
    cur = conn.execute(f"INSERT INTO translations ({','.join(row)}) VALUES ({','.join('?' * len(row))})",
                       list(row.values()))
    return cur.lastrowid, True


def request_translation(source_table, source_column, source_row_key, target_language, stage, due_stage=None, *,
                        session, dry_run=False, contract_path=None):
    """Ask for a translation of one cell. The cell is read here and only its hash is stored: no argument carries
    the original. Refused: a pointer that does not resolve (no such table or column, a table with no single-column
    primary key, no such row, a cell that is not text or is empty), a target language lang_jur_map does not hold or
    that is the pointed row's own language, a stage that is not a stage id of the contract, and a cell that already
    has a current translation into that language (the refusal names `--supersedes`)."""
    _require_translation_session(session, "request-translation")
    contract = _translation_contract(contract_path)
    with connect(dry_run) as conn:
        tid, created = _open_translation_request(conn, source_table, source_column, source_row_key, target_language,
                                                 stage, due_stage, contract, session, "request-translation")
    return {"translation_id": tid, "created": created, "status": "requested", "dry_run": dry_run}


def record_translation(text, translator_kind, translator_name, *, translation_id=None, source_table=None,
                       source_column=None, source_row_key=None, target_language=None, stage=None, due_stage=None,
                       supersedes=None, session, dry_run=False, contract_path=None):
    """Answer a request by id, or open and answer one in one call by pointer (exactly one of the two forms).

    Refused: both forms or neither; a translation that adds, drops or changes a number of the original
    (`translation_number_gaps`); a cell whose hash no longer matches the request's (request it again); a request
    that is not `requested`. `--supersedes M` retires translation M in place, in the same transaction; it is refused
    unless M is translated or reviewed, not already retired, and translates the same pointer into the same language.
    The original is never touched."""
    ctx = "record-translation"
    _require_translation_session(session, ctx)
    pointer = (source_table, source_column, source_row_key, target_language, stage)
    if translation_id is not None and any(p is not None for p in pointer + (due_stage,)):
        raise Refusal(f"{ctx}: pass --translation-id OR the pointer (--source-table, --source-column, "
                      f"--source-row-id, --target-language, --stage), never both. Nothing was written.")
    if translation_id is None and not all((p or "").strip() for p in pointer):
        raise Refusal(f"{ctx}: pass --translation-id, or the whole pointer: --source-table, --source-column, "
                      f"--source-row-id, --target-language and --stage. Nothing was written.")
    text, name = (text or "").strip(), (translator_name or "").strip()
    if not text:
        raise Refusal(f"{ctx}: --text is blank. Nothing was written.")
    if not name:
        raise Refusal(f"{ctx}: --translator-name is required: the model id, the tool and version, or the person. "
                      f"Nothing was written.")
    contract = _translation_contract(contract_path)
    with connect(dry_run) as conn:
        dbcore.check_declared(conn, "translations", "translator_kind", translator_kind, ctx)
        old = None
        if supersedes is not None:
            old = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM translations WHERE translation_id=?", (supersedes,)).fetchone()
            if not old or old["status"] not in ("translated", "reviewed") or old["superseded_by_translation_id"]:
                raise Refusal(f"{ctx}: --supersedes {supersedes} is not a current translation (translated or "
                              f"reviewed, and not already retired). Nothing was written.")
        if translation_id is None:
            tid, _ = _open_translation_request(conn, source_table, source_column, source_row_key, target_language,
                                               stage, due_stage, contract, session, ctx, replacing=supersedes)
        else:
            tid = translation_id
        req = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM translations WHERE translation_id=?", (tid,)).fetchone()
        if not req:
            raise Refusal(f"{ctx}: no translation request {tid}. Nothing was written.")
        if req["status"] != "requested":
            raise Refusal(f"{ctx}: translation {tid} is {req['status']}, not requested. A corrected translation "
                          f"is a new row: record it against the pointer with --supersedes {tid}. "
                          f"Nothing was written.")
        where = (req["source_table"], req["source_column"], req["source_row_key"], req["target_language"])
        _refuse_retired_cell(conn, where[0], where[2], ctx)
        if old and (old["source_table"], old["source_column"], old["source_row_key"],
                    old["target_language"]) != where:
            raise Refusal(f"{ctx}: --supersedes {supersedes} translates a different cell or language. "
                          f"Nothing was written.")
        _refuse_second_translation(conn, *where, supersedes, ctx)
        original, _, why = dbcore.read_cell(conn, *where[:3])
        if why:
            raise Refusal(f"{ctx}: the pointer no longer resolves: {why}. Nothing was written.")
        if translation_sha256(original) != req["source_sha256"]:
            raise Refusal(f"{ctx}: the original cell has changed since request {tid} was made (its hash no longer "
                          f"matches). Request the translation again. Nothing was written.")
        dropped, added = translation_number_gaps(original, text, translation_claimed_value(conn, *where[:3]))
        if dropped or added:
            raise Refusal(f"{ctx}: the translation does not state the original's numbers. Dropped: "
                          f"{dropped or 'none'}; added: {added or 'none'}. Every number the original states as a "
                          f"numeral is stated in the translation, and every number the translation states is the "
                          f"original's (or the figure's verified claimed_value). Nothing was written.")
        stamp = dbcore.upd(session)
        conn.execute("UPDATE translations SET translated_text=?, status='translated', translator_kind=?, "
                     "translator_name=?, updated_at=?, updated_by_session=? WHERE translation_id=?",
                     (text, translator_kind, name, stamp["updated_at"], stamp["updated_by_session"], tid))
        if old:
            conn.execute("UPDATE translations SET superseded_by_translation_id=?, updated_at=?, "
                         "updated_by_session=? WHERE translation_id=?",
                         (tid, stamp["updated_at"], stamp["updated_by_session"], supersedes))
    return {"translation_id": tid, "status": "translated", "supersedes": supersedes, "dry_run": dry_run}


def review_translation(translation_id, verdict, reviewer_kind, reviewer_name, reason=None, *, session,
                       dry_run=False):
    """Review a translation: `reviewed` (a reader may be shown it) or `rejected` (`--reason` required, written to
    `review_reason`). OD-30: a translation shown to a reader is reviewed by an Opus-class instance other than its
    translator; the database records the reviewer's name and cannot verify its class, and render shows only
    `reviewed` rows. Refused: a verdict other than the two statuses a review sets, a blank reviewer, the translator
    as reviewer (compared case-insensitively), a row that is not `translated` or is retired, and a `reviewed`
    verdict on a cell whose hash no longer matches (reject it and request again)."""
    ctx = "review-translation"
    _require_translation_session(session, ctx)
    if verdict not in ("reviewed", "rejected"):
        raise Refusal(f"{ctx}: --verdict is reviewed or rejected, not {verdict!r}. Nothing was written.")
    name, reason = (reviewer_name or "").strip(), (reason or "").strip() or None
    if not name:
        raise Refusal(f"{ctx}: --reviewer-name is required: the model id, the tool or the person who reviewed it. "
                      f"Nothing was written.")
    if verdict == "rejected" and not reason:
        raise Refusal(f"{ctx}: --reason is required to reject a translation. Nothing was written.")
    with connect(dry_run) as conn:
        dbcore.check_declared(conn, "translations", "reviewed_by_kind", reviewer_kind, ctx)
        row = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM translations WHERE translation_id=?", (translation_id,)).fetchone()
        if not row:
            raise Refusal(f"{ctx}: no translation {translation_id}. Nothing was written.")
        if row["status"] != "translated" or row["superseded_by_translation_id"]:
            raise Refusal(f"{ctx}: translation {translation_id} is {row['status']}"
                          f"{' and retired' if row['superseded_by_translation_id'] else ''}; only a translated, "
                          f"current translation is reviewed. Nothing was written.")
        _refuse_retired_cell(conn, row["source_table"], row["source_row_key"], ctx)
        if name.casefold() == row["translator_name"].casefold():
            raise Refusal(f"{ctx}: the reviewer ({name}) is the translator. A translation shown to a reader is "
                          f"reviewed by an Opus-class instance other than its translator (OD-30). "
                          f"Nothing was written.")
        if verdict == "reviewed":
            original, _, why = dbcore.read_cell(conn, row["source_table"], row["source_column"],
                                                row["source_row_key"])
            if why or translation_sha256(original) != row["source_sha256"]:
                raise Refusal(f"{ctx}: the original cell no longer matches the one translated "
                              f"({why or 'its hash changed'}). Reject this translation and request it again. "
                              f"Nothing was written.")
        stamp = dbcore.upd(session)
        conn.execute("UPDATE translations SET status=?, reviewed_by_kind=?, reviewed_by_name=?, reviewed_at=?, "
                     "review_reason=?, updated_at=?, updated_by_session=? WHERE translation_id=?",
                     (verdict, reviewer_kind, name, stamp["updated_at"], reason, stamp["updated_at"],
                      stamp["updated_by_session"], translation_id))
    return {"translation_id": translation_id, "status": verdict, "dry_run": dry_run}


def translations_due(stage, contract_path=None):
    """The open requests (`requested`, not retired) that fall due at `stage`: the row's own `due_stage` where it has
    one, else the translation rule's default stage, read from the contract when asked and never stored. Refused when
    the contract holds no translation rule."""
    contract = _translation_contract(contract_path)
    _translation_stage(contract, stage, "--due-at")
    if contract.translation is None:
        raise Refusal("governance/pipeline-contract.yaml holds no translation rule, so no request has a default "
                      "stage. Nothing was read.")
    default = contract.translation.default_stage
    with connect(readonly=True) as conn:
        rows = conn.execute(
            "SELECT translation_id, source_table, source_column, source_row_key, target_language, "
            "requested_at_stage, due_stage FROM translations "
            "WHERE status='requested' AND superseded_by_translation_id IS NULL "
            # a request on a retired figure is not owed (retire-extraction); the row stays as history
            "AND NOT (source_table = 'source_value_extractions' AND source_row_key IN "
            "(SELECT CAST(extraction_id AS TEXT) FROM source_value_extractions WHERE retired_at IS NOT NULL)) "
            "ORDER BY translation_id").fetchall()
    return [dict(r, due_stage=r["due_stage"] or default, due_by="row" if r["due_stage"] else "rule")
            for r in rows if (r["due_stage"] or default) == stage]


if __name__ == "__main__":
    # REFUSALS ARE MESSAGES, NOT STACK TRACES. This CLI's whole value is that it says no
    # (CLAUDE.md §4), and its refusals are careful: they cite the ruling, name the remedy
    # and say what was written, which is nothing. Every one of them reached the terminal
    # as the last line of a traceback until 2026-09-10 -- the message at the bottom of a
    # stack the operator did not ask for and has to read past. Same refusals, same exit 1,
    # no stack. Refusal only: anything else keeps its traceback, because anything else is
    # a defect and its location is the evidence.
    try:
        main()
    except Refusal as exc:
        _record(str(exc))
        sys.exit(f"REFUSING: {exc}")
    except Exception as exc:   # a defect, kept and then raised unchanged: traceback and exit code are the evidence
        _record(f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")
        raise

    p_amt.add_argument("--session", required=True)
    p_amt.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")

    p_ams = sub.add_parser("amend-source",
                           help="Correct a JUDGEMENT field on an evidence row, recording what was replaced")
    p_ams.add_argument("--ref-id", required=True)
    p_ams.add_argument("--field", required=True,
                       help="A judgement field, not a bibliographic one. Bibliographic "
                            "fields belong to correct-source and are refused here.")
    p_ams.add_argument("--replacement", required=True)
    p_ams.add_argument("--reason", required=True,
                       help="Why the previous text was wrong. Recorded in "
                            "metadata_integrity_detail with the replaced text.")
    p_ams.add_argument("--tier", type=int, default=None,
                       help="Optional with --field scope or --field evidence_type: the tier "
                            "moves to the one value the ratified ladder derives, in the "
                            "same statement, and a value that disagrees is refused. The "
                            "tier is never set on its own.")
    p_ams.add_argument("--scope", default=None,
                       help="Only with --field evidence_type: the scope the new tier is "
                            "derived from. Required when the new type spans more than one "
                            "tier; derived when it admits exactly one.")
    p_ams.add_argument("--co1-provenance", default=None,
                       help="Only with --field evidence_type --replacement co1, and "
                            "required there: the D-0178 warrant naming the co-production. "
                            "A move OFF co1 keeps the old warrant in the ledger and NULLs "
                            "the column.")
    p_ams.add_argument("--co1-source-type", default=None,
                       help="Only with --field evidence_type --replacement co1, and "
                            "required there: a member of schemas.enums.Co1SourceType. "
                            "grain_for grades a Co-1 source's grain from it.")
    p_ams.add_argument("--session", required=True)
    elif args.command == "amend-term":
        _emit(amend_term(args.term_id, args.field, args.replacement, args.reason,
                         session=args.session, dry_run=args.dry_run))

    elif args.command == "amend-source":
        _emit(amend_source(args.ref_id, args.field, args.replacement, args.reason,
                           session=args.session, dry_run=args.dry_run,
                           tier=args.tier, scope=args.scope,
                           co1_provenance=args.co1_provenance,
                           co1_source_type=args.co1_source_type))

    source_type = (co1_source_type or "").strip()
    if new_type != "co1" and co1_source_type is not None:
        raise Refusal(
            f"{ref_id}: --co1-source-type is only admissible when the new evidence_type "
            f"is co1; {new_type!r} carries no Co-1 source type. Nothing was written.")
    if new_type == "co1":
        from schemas.enums import Co1SourceType  # noqa: E402
        members = sorted(m.value for m in Co1SourceType)
        if not source_type:
            raise Refusal(
                f"{ref_id}: --co1-source-type is REQUIRED to move evidence_type to co1. "
                f"A Co-1 row needs it (co1_field_consistency), and grain_for grades the "
                f"source's grain from it: left NULL, a community-consensus source reads as "
                f"one person's account. Choose from schemas.enums.Co1SourceType: "
                f"{members}. Nothing was written.")
        if source_type not in members:
            raise Refusal(
                f"{ref_id}: --co1-source-type {source_type!r} is not a member of "
                f"schemas.enums.Co1SourceType: {members}. Nothing was written.")
    sets = {"scope": scope, "tier": derived}
    moved_scope = (f"scope {cur['scope']!r} unchanged" if cur["scope"] == scope
                   else f"scope {cur['scope']!r} -> {scope!r}")
    text = (f". {moved_scope}; tier {cur['tier']} -> {derived}, derived from "
            f"(evidence_type, scope) by the ratified ladder in the same statement as the "
            f"type.")
    if new_type == "co1":
        sets["co1_provenance"] = provenance
        sets["co1_source_type"] = source_type
        text += (f" co1_provenance written as the D-0178 warrant; replaced text was: "
                 f"{cur['co1_provenance']!r}. co1_source_type written as "
                 f"{source_type!r}; replaced value was {cur['co1_source_type']!r}.")
    leaving = (old_type or "").strip().lower() == "co1"
    moved = {c: cur[c] for c in co1_cols if leaving and cur[c] is not None}
    if moved:
        sets.update({c: None for c in moved})
        text += (" Leaving co1, so the Co-1-only fields are set NULL and their text is "
                 "kept here: " + "; ".join(f"{c} was {v!r}" for c, v in moved.items())
                 + ".")
    out = {"type_was": old_type, "type_now": new_type, "scope_was": cur["scope"],
           "scope_now": scope, "tier_was": cur["tier"], "tier_now": derived,
           "nulled": sorted(moved)}
    return {"sets": sets, "ledger": text, "out": out}


def amend_source(ref_id: str, field: str, replacement: str, reason: str,
                 session: str, dry_run: bool = False, tier=None, scope=None,
                 co1_provenance=None, co1_source_type=None):
    """Replace a JUDGEMENT field on an evidence row, recording what was replaced.

    Replaces rather than appends, and that is the opposite of what resolve-candidate
    and amend-search do, on purpose. Those fields hold a HYPOTHESIS, and R15 wants the
    guess left legible beside the correction. These fields hold a WARRANT -- the
    sentence a downstream reader takes as the reason a source stands where it does. A
    false citation inside co1_provenance is not a historical record of what someone
    believed; it is a live claim about why a Co-1 source counts as Co-1, and leaving
    it in place with a correction underneath means the next reader can still quote it.

    So the wrong text goes, and it goes into metadata_integrity_detail with the date
    and the reason, where it is preserved without being quotable as the warrant.

    Written 2026-09-02 for REF-00978, whose co1_provenance ended "Provenance verified
    from the retrieved report itself (p.2, p.28), not from a description of it." p.2 of
    that PDF is blank, p.28 is survey question 40, and the charity number the sentence
    carried appears nowhere in the 29 pages -- it came from a web description, which is
    the one thing the sentence denies. A verification assertion that is itself the
    thing that failed is the CLAUDE.md 2(c) shape, and it was in the field carrying a
    CRPD Art 4.3 warrant.

                 a.get("is_corporate", 0), a.get("corporate_name"),

    return data["ref_id"]


# Fields `correct-source` can rewrite. The boundary is not a taste judgement: it is
# EXACTLY what retrieval_log --verify-authors can prove against a payload. A field the
# verifier cannot check is a field this writer must not touch, or the repository gains
# a way to assert a bibliographic value that nothing can ever contradict.
def _correctable():
    """The payload-backed columns, DERIVED from the verifier's own map.

    Not a second list. `_BIBLIO_FIELDS` in retrieval_log is what --verify-authors can
    actually prove against a payload, and this dict's contract is to be exactly that set
    -- so it is that set, plus `pub_title`, which the verifier checks through `_TITLE_COLS`
    instead (the verifier compares a SET of title columns where this writer targets one).
    That exception is stated here rather than left implicit.
    """
    retrieval_log = _retrieval_log()
    out = {"pub_title": lambda m: next((t for t in (m.get("title") or []) if t), None)}
    out.update(dict(retrieval_log.PAYLOAD_FIELDS))
    return out


_CORRECTABLE = _correctable()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The typed home for translations (T-049): AT-107, AT-108, AT-109, each shown to fire and to pass.

WHAT REACHES THE GUIDEBOOK WITHOUT THESE CASES. A session that meets a Japanese or Dutch quotation either translates
in its head and loses the translation, or writes an English paraphrase where the source's words should be and a
later reader takes it for the source's. A translation that adds, drops or changes a figure passes every gate that asks
only whether a translation EXISTS. A translation shown beside a quotation that has since changed. A stage name
written into a verb's code, so that moving the default is a code change.

AT-107  from the stage judgment, request and record a translation of a non-English figure's claim_text by the verbs
        alone: the original cell is byte-identical, the current-translations view joins back to it by its pointer,
        requested_at_stage is judgment, and the verbs change no file under scripts/ or schemas/.
AT-108  with the contract as committed a request with no --due-stage is listed at the contract's default stage; with
        a temporary copy of the contract naming another stage it is listed there and not at the first, and a request
        that names its own due stage is listed there under both; no file is changed; no stage id is written as a
        string constant inside the verbs.
AT-109  a translation that changes a figure of the original is refused; one that drops a figure is refused; one that
        keeps every figure is accepted; one of a quote that spells its number in words, stating the numeral of the
        row's claimed_value, is accepted; one of a quote in CJK numerals, stating them as Arabic numerals, is
        accepted. A pointer to a table, column or row that does not exist, or into a table whose key has several
        columns, is refused; the original cannot be retyped; a cell changed since the request is refused; review
        needs a reviewer other than the translator and a reason to reject; the schema holds the review rules itself;
        --supersedes retires the translation it names and refuses what it should.

Every probe is chosen by query. Anything written goes to a COPY of the database (rows marked TASK-FIXTURE); a state
the verbs cannot build is made by SQL on a second copy and marked HAND. A case that needs a state the live data does
not offer prints SKIPPED-NO-FIXTURE (counted apart), never silently passes.
"""
import ast
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import sqlite3
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

import yaml

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
os.chdir(REPO)
TMP = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="guidebook-t049-")
DB = os.path.join(TMP, "guidebook.db")
shutil.copy(REPO / "data" / "guidebook.db", DB)
os.environ["GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH"] = DB
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO / "scripts"))
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO))
import db                                                              # noqa: E402
import dbcore                                                          # noqa: E402
from dbcore import Refusal                                             # noqa: E402
from schemas.pipeline_contract import PipelineContract                 # noqa: E402

S = "session_test-translations"
CONTRACT_FILE = REPO / "governance" / "pipeline-contract.yaml"
results, skipped = [], []


def record(tid, name, passed, details=""):
    results.append(bool(passed))
    print(f"  [{'✓' if passed else '✗'}] {tid}: {name}")
    if details and not passed:
        print(f"      {str(details)[:500]}")


def skip(tid, why):
    skipped.append(tid)
    print(f"  [-] {tid}: SKIPPED-NO-FIXTURE: {why}")


def refused_for(part, fn, *a, **k):
    """True when `fn` refuses AND the refusal says `part`: refused for the reason under test, not another."""
    try:
        fn(*a, **k)
    except Refusal as exc:
        return part in str(exc)
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
        print(f"      DEFECT (not a refusal): {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")
    return False


def cli(*args, path=None):
    p = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "scripts/db.py", *args], capture_output=True, text=True,
                       env={**os.environ, "GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH": path or DB})
    return p.returncode, p.stdout, p.stderr


def finish():
    print(f"\nEXAMINED: {len(results)} cases")
    print(f"SKIPPED-NO-FIXTURE: {len(skipped)}")
    ok = bool(results) and all(results)
    if ok:
        shutil.rmtree(TMP, ignore_errors=True)
    else:
        print(f"FAILED: {results.count(False)}   (scratch kept: {TMP})")
    print("PASS" if ok else "FAIL")
    sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)


def tracked_state():
    return subprocess.run(["git", "status", "--porcelain", "scripts", "schemas"], capture_output=True,
                          text=True).stdout


con = sqlite3.connect(DB)
con.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
q = lambda sql, *p: con.execute(sql, p).fetchall()  # noqa: E731

# --- the schema and the verbs exist: absent, every case below is red by name ---------------------------------------
have = q("SELECT count(*) FROM sqlite_master WHERE name IN ('translations', 'v_translations_current')")[0][0] == 2
verbs = all(hasattr(db, f) for f in ("request_translation", "record_translation", "review_translation",
                                     "translations_due"))
record("T049-01", "the translations table, its current view and the four verbs exist", have and verbs,
       f"table+view: {have}, verbs: {verbs}")
if not (have and verbs):
    finish()

CONTRACT = PipelineContract.load(CONTRACT_FILE)
STAGES = [st.id for st in CONTRACT.stages]
if not plain or not JUDGMENT:
    skip("T049-10", f"no non-English figure with plain integers (plain={bool(plain)}, judgment={bool(JUDGMENT)})")
else:
    L1, L2, L3, L4 = langs_for(plain, 4)
    before_cell, before_tree = cell(plain), tracked_state()
    text = "TASK-FIXTURE " + " ".join(NUM.findall(plain["text"]))
    rc1, out1, err1 = cli("request-translation", *ptr(plain, L1), "--stage", JUDGMENT, "--session", S)
    tid = json.loads(out1)["translation_id"] if rc1 == 0 else None
    listed_default = [r["translation_id"] for r in json.loads(cli("translations", "--due-at", DEFAULT)[1] or "[]")]
    rc2, out2, err2 = cli("record-translation", "--translation-id", str(tid), "--text", text,
                          "--translator-kind", "model", "--translator-name", "test-translator", "--session", S)
    record("T049-10", "AT-107 request and record by the verbs alone", rc1 == 0 and rc2 == 0, err1 + err2)
    record("T049-11", "AT-107 the original cell is byte-identical", cell(plain) == before_cell)
    joined = q("SELECT v.translation_id, v.translated_text FROM v_translations_current v "
               "JOIN source_value_extractions x ON v.source_table='source_value_extractions' "
               "AND v.source_column='claim_text' AND v.source_row_key=CAST(x.extraction_id AS TEXT) "
               "WHERE x.extraction_id=? AND x.claim_text=?", plain["id"], before_cell)
    record("T049-12", "AT-107 the current view joins back to that cell by its pointer",
           [tuple(r) for r in joined] == [(tid, text)], joined)
    record("T049-13", "AT-107 requested_at_stage is judgment",
           q("SELECT requested_at_stage FROM translations WHERE translation_id=?", tid)[0][0] == JUDGMENT)
    record("T049-14", "AT-107 the verbs changed no file under scripts/ or schemas/ (the porcelain is the same "
                      "before and after them)", tracked_state() == before_tree)

    # === AT-108 ===========================================================================================
    record("T049-20", "AT-108 an unforced request is listed at the contract's default stage while it is open",
           tid in listed_default, listed_default)
    rq = db.request_translation("source_value_extractions", "claim_text", str(plain["id"]), L2, JUDGMENT, session=S)
    rq_due = db.request_translation("source_value_extractions", "claim_text", str(plain["id"]), L3, JUDGMENT,
                                    due_stage=THIRD, session=S)
    alt = Path(TMP) / "contract-alt.yaml"
    alt.write_text(re.sub(r"(?m)^(  default_stage: ).*$", rf"\g<1>{OTHER}", CONTRACT_FILE.read_text(encoding="utf-8")))
    nokey = Path(TMP) / "contract-no-rule.yaml"
    d = yaml.safe_load(CONTRACT_FILE.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    del d["translation"]
    nokey.write_text(yaml.safe_dump(d, sort_keys=False))
    tree = tracked_state()
    ids = lambda stage, **k: [r["translation_id"] for r in db.translations_due(stage, **k)]  # noqa: E731
    record("T049-21", "AT-108 the open request is listed at the default stage and at no other",
           rq["translation_id"] in ids(DEFAULT) and rq["translation_id"] not in ids(OTHER), ids(DEFAULT))
    record("T049-22", "AT-108 a copy of the contract naming another stage lists it there and not at the first",
           rq["translation_id"] in ids(OTHER, contract_path=alt) and rq["translation_id"] not in
           ids(DEFAULT, contract_path=alt), (ids(OTHER, contract_path=alt), ids(DEFAULT, contract_path=alt)))
    record("T049-23", "AT-108 a request with its own --due-stage is listed there under both contracts, not at the "
                      "default",
           all(rq_due["translation_id"] in ids(THIRD, contract_path=c) for c in (CONTRACT_FILE, alt))
           and rq_due["translation_id"] not in ids(DEFAULT) + ids(OTHER, contract_path=alt))
    record("T049-24", "AT-108 moving the default changed no file under scripts/ or schemas/",
           tracked_state() == tree)
    record("T049-25", "the lister refuses when the contract holds no translation rule",
           refused_for("no translation rule", db.translations_due, DEFAULT, contract_path=nokey))
    record("T049-26", "the lister refuses a stage the contract does not hold",
           refused_for("is not a stage id", db.translations_due, "no-such-stage-t049"))
    bad = dict(d, translation={"default_stage": "no-such-stage-t049"})
    try:
        PipelineContract.model_validate(bad)
        refused_model = False
    except ValueError:
        refused_model = True
    record("T049-27", "the contract model refuses a default stage that is not one of its own stages", refused_model)
    record("T049-28", "a stage that is not a stage id is refused as --stage and as --due-stage",
           refused_for("is not a stage id", db.request_translation, "source_value_extractions", "claim_text",
                       str(plain["id"]), L4, "no-such-stage-t049", session=S)
           and refused_for("is not a stage id", db.request_translation, "source_value_extractions", "claim_text",
                           str(plain["id"]), L4, JUDGMENT, due_stage="no-such-stage-t049", session=S))

# no stage id is a string constant inside the verbs: the block this task adds to db.py, from its header to the end
src = Path(db.__file__).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
header = src.index("# --- translations (T-049)")
head_line = src.count("\n", 0, header) + 1
fns = [n for n in ast.parse(src).body if isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef) and n.lineno > head_line]
literal = [(fn.name, n.value) for fn in fns for n in ast.walk(fn)
           if isinstance(n, ast.Constant) and isinstance(n.value, str) and n.value in STAGES]
record("T049-29", "AT-108 no stage id is a string constant in the translation verbs and their helpers",
       {"request_translation", "record_translation", "review_translation", "translations_due"}
       <= {fn.name for fn in fns} and not literal, literal)

# === AT-109 ===============================================================================================
KW = dict(translator_kind="model", translator_name="test-translator", session=S)
if not plain:
    skip("T049-30", "no non-English figure with plain integers")

# attempt_count=1 for any VERIFIED row, reasoning that it was avoiding a row
    # the blocking invariants reject. It did the opposite twice over: `tool`
    # carries the contract "verified_by_tool names which", so the row failed I4b
    # anyway — and, worse, the defaults were INVENTED FACTS. No tool ran; no
    # attempt happened. A write path that manufactures an audit trail to satisfy
    # an audit is a doctrine violation in a project whose stated epistemics are
    # "I don't know" over invention, and it would have laundered fabricated
    # provenance into the one column that exists to record how a standing was
    # reached. Refusal is symmetrical with the R9 duplicate errors below.
    vs = data.get("verification_status")
    if vs == "VERIFIED":
        if not data.get("verification_method"):
            raise Refusal(
                "VERIFIED requires --verification-method (how it was established: "
                "tool / corroborated-not-retrieved / co1-attestation / "
                "citing-bibliography). D-0157: a standing without its method is "
                "not a standing. Filing it as UNVERIFIED with disposition OPEN is "
                "the honest move if you have not established it.")
        if data["verification_method"] == "tool" and not data.get("verified_by_tool"):
            raise Refusal(
                "verification_method='tool' requires --verified-by-tool naming "
                "which tool established it (invariant I4b).")
        data.setdefault("verification_attempt_count", 1)
        # D-0157 invariant I1: "verification is finished or it did not happen."
        # insert_source set OPEN unconditionally, so EVERY verified source it wrote
        # failed I1 the moment anything looked. That went unnoticed while
        # evidence_sources held 0 rows and I1 was vacuous; this batch is the first to
        # repopulate it, and all nine rows failed together. A default that no row can
        # satisfy is not a default, it is a trap.
        data.setdefault("verification_disposition", "CLOSED")
    elif vs == "UNVERIFIED":
        data.setdefault("verification_disposition", "OPEN")
        data.setdefault("verification_attempt_count", 1)
